I'm working on a CUE code generator for component definitions that handles optional collection parameters like lists and maps.

*   Length conditions (LenEq, LenGt, LenGte, LenLt, LenLte) on StringParam, ArrayParam, and MapParam must generate CUE using bracket-access chained-guard syntax: `parameter["name"] != _|_ if len(parameter["name"]) <op> <n>` — NOT the old dot-syntax `len(parameter.name) <op> <n>`.

*   ArrayParam.Contains(val) must generate `parameter["name"] != _|_ if list.Contains(parameter["name"], val)` — NOT `list.Contains(parameter.name, val)`.

*   MapParam.HasKey(key) must generate `parameter["name"] != _|_ && parameter["name"].key != _|_` — NOT `parameter.name.key != _|_`.

*   ArrayParam.IsEmpty() and MapParam.IsEmpty() (and LenEq(0) on both) must return an AbsentOrEmptyCondition. At render time (SetIf, SpreadIf, validator FailWhen/OnlyWhen), this condition expands into TWO separate if blocks: one for `parameter["name"] == _|_` (absent branch) and one for `parameter["name"] != _|_ if len(parameter["name"]) == 0` (set-and-empty branch), each emitting the same body.

*   ArrayParam.IsNotEmpty() and MapParam.IsNotEmpty() must generate `parameter["name"] != _|_ if len(parameter["name"]) > 0`.

*   AllConditions(...) must join conditions with ` if ` when any sub-condition uses chained-guard syntax (LenCondition, ArrayContainsCondition); for non-chained conditions only, it joins with ` && `.

*   Logical OR (using Or()) must always join conditions with ` || ` regardless of whether any operand uses chained-guard syntax.

*   When an And/AllConditions compound includes a LenCondition or ArrayContainsCondition operand, the compound must NOT wrap the chained-guard operand in `(...) && (...)` form.

*   When a OneOf parameter has both Optional() and a Default value set, the generated parameter schema must render the discriminator field as `fieldName: *"default" | "other"` (concrete, no `?` marker). When Optional() is set without a Default, the `?` marker must appear.

*   ArrayParam.RequiredImports() must return ["list"] when MinItems or MaxItems is set, and nil when neither is set. If both are set, ["list"] is returned exactly once. The CUE generator must auto-import "list" based on this method.

*   StringKeyMapParam must expose HasKey(key string) Condition, IsEmpty() Condition, IsNotEmpty() Condition, LenEq(n int) Condition, and LenGt(n int) Condition methods mirroring MapParam's predicates.

*   StringKeyMapParam.HasKey(key) must return a *MapHasKeyCondition with ParamName() returning the parameter name and Key() returning the key argument.

*   When SetIf uses a bracket-access path (e.g. "data[key-name]") with a single condition, the bracket key must be rendered inside a guarded if block. With an AbsentOrEmpty condition, two if blocks are emitted (one per branch). An unconditional Set with a bracket-access path must render without any if block.

*   A bracket-access path that has nested children (e.g. "metadata.annotations[key].nested") must render as a quoted struct: `"key": { nested: ... }`.

*   FailWhen(coll.IsEmpty()) in a validator must emit two false-assignment blocks (one per AbsentOrEmpty branch). OnlyWhen(coll.IsEmpty()) must duplicate the entire validator body under both branches.

19	// Validator represents a CUE _validate* block pattern used for cross-field validation.
20	// Validators emit blocks like:
21	//
22	//	_validateTenantName: {
23	//	    "tenantName must not end with a hyphen": true
24	//	    if tenantName =~ ".*-$" {
25	//	        "tenantName must not end with a hyphen": false
26	//	    }
27	//	}
28	//
29	// Validators can be guarded (only active when a condition is true) and can be attached
30	// at different levels: top-level parameter, inside map/struct params, or inside array elements.
31	type Validator struct {
32		message   string    // the validation message (used as CUE field key)
33		failCond  Condition // when this condition is true, validation fails
34		guardCond Condition // optional: validator only active when guard is true
35		name      string    // optional: override the CUE variable name (default: derived from message)
36	}
37	
38	// Validate creates a new Validator with the given error message.
39	// The message is used both as the CUE field key and as the error shown on failure.
40	func Validate(message string) *Validator {
41		return &Validator{message: message}
42	}
43	
44	// FailWhen sets the condition that causes validation to fail.
45	// When this condition evaluates to true, the validator emits false for the message key.
46	func (v *Validator) FailWhen(cond Condition) *Validator {
47		v.failCond = cond
48		return v
49	}
50	
51	// OnlyWhen sets a guard condition — the validator is only active when this condition is true.
52	// If the guard condition is false, the entire validator block is skipped.
53	func (v *Validator) OnlyWhen(guard Condition) *Validator {
54		v.guardCond = guard
55		return v
56	}
57	
58	// WithName overrides the CUE variable name for the validator block.
59	// By default, the name is derived from the message (e.g., "_validateTenantName").
60	func (v *Validator) WithName(name string) *Validator {
61		v.name = name
62		return v
63	}
64	
65	// Message returns the validation message.
66	func (v *Validator) Message() string { return v.message }
67	
68	// FailCondition returns the fail condition.
69	func (v *Validator) FailCondition() Condition { return v.failCond }
70	
71	// GuardCondition returns the guard condition, or nil if not set.
72	func (v *Validator) GuardCondition() Condition { return v.guardCond }
73	
74	// CUEName returns the CUE variable name for this validator.
75	func (v *Validator) CUEName() string { return v.name }

77	// LocalField creates a reference to a field in the current CUE scope (no "parameter." prefix).
78	// Used inside validators for condition-building on sibling fields.
79	// The name is emitted verbatim — supports dot-paths ("Principal.AWS")
80	// and array indexing ("expiration[0].date").
81	//
82	// Compare with defkit.String("name") / defkit.Bool("name") which reference
83	// top-level parameters and emit "parameter.name" in CUE.
84	//
85	// Example: LocalField("tenantName").Matches(".*-$")
86	func LocalField(name string) *LocalFieldRef {
87		return &LocalFieldRef{fieldName: name}
88	}

90	// LocalFieldRef represents a reference to a field within the current scope.
91	// It implements Value so it can be used with upstream Comparison, LenValueCondition, etc.
92	// It provides ergonomic condition builder methods: Matches(), Eq(), IsSet(), LenEq(), Gte(), etc.
93	type LocalFieldRef struct {
94		fieldName string
95	}
96	
97	// Value/Expr interface implementation — allows LocalFieldRef to be used
98	// with upstream types like Comparison, LenValueCondition, etc.
99	func (s *LocalFieldRef) expr()  {}
100	func (s *LocalFieldRef) value() {}
101	
102	// Name returns the field name.
103	func (s *LocalFieldRef) Name() string { return s.fieldName }
104	
105	// Matches creates a condition that checks if this field matches a regex pattern.
106	// Example: LocalField("tenantName").Matches(".*-$") generates: tenantName =~ ".*-$"
107	// Reuses upstream RegexMatchCondition.
108	func (s *LocalFieldRef) Matches(pattern string) Condition {
109		return RegexMatch(s, pattern)
110	}
111	
112	// Eq creates a condition comparing this field to a value.
113	// Example: LocalField("type").Eq("aws") generates: type == "aws"
114	// Reuses upstream Comparison type.
115	func (s *LocalFieldRef) Eq(val any) Condition {
116		return Eq(s, Lit(val))
117	}
118	
119	// Ne creates a condition checking this field is not equal to a value.
120	// Reuses upstream Comparison type.
121	func (s *LocalFieldRef) Ne(val any) Condition {
122		return Ne(s, Lit(val))
123	}
124	
125	// IsSet creates a condition that checks if this field has a value (not bottom).
126	// Example: LocalField("role").IsSet() generates: role != _|_
127	// Reuses upstream PathExistsCondition.
128	func (s *LocalFieldRef) IsSet() Condition {
129		return PathExists(s.fieldName)
130	}
131	
132	// NotSet creates a condition that checks if this field is not set (is bottom).

136	}

139	// Example: LocalField("Principal.AWS").LenEq(0) generates: len(Principal.AWS) == 0
140	// Reuses upstream LenValueCondition via LenEq().
141	func (s *LocalFieldRef) LenEq(n int) Condition {

157	// Example: LocalField("days").Gte(LocalField("expiration[0].days"))

169	type LenOfExpr struct {

173	// LenOf creates a length expression wrapper around any Value.
174	func LenOf(v Value) *LenOfExpr {

183	// Gte creates a condition: len(inner) >= n. Returns upstream *LenValueCondition.

185		return LenGe(l.inner, n)
186	}
187	
188	// Eq creates a condition: len(inner) == n. Returns upstream *LenValueCondition.
189	func (l *LenOfExpr) Eq(n int) Condition {
190		return LenEq(l.inner, n)
191	}

**`expr.go`**
- Added the exported `AbsentOrEmptyCondition` type with `ParamName() string` and `Branches() []Condition`. `Branches()` returns the absent branch (`Not(IsSet)`) and the set-and-empty branch (`LenCondition{==,0}`).
- Updated doc comments on `LenCondition`, `ArrayContainsCondition`, `MapHasKeyCondition` to reflect the new bracket-chained syntax.

**`param.go`**
- `ArrayParam.IsEmpty()`, `MapParam.IsEmpty()`, and `LenEq(0)` on both now return `*AbsentOrEmptyCondition`; `IsNotEmpty()` stays a `LenCondition{>,0}`.
- Added `ArrayParam.RequiredImports()` → `["list"]` when `MinItems` or `MaxItems` is set (exactly once even if both), else `nil`.
- Added `StringKeyMapParam` predicates: `HasKey` (returns `*MapHasKeyCondition`), `IsEmpty`, `IsNotEmpty`, `LenEq` (0 → AbsentOrEmpty), `LenGt`.

**`cuegen.go`**
- `conditionToCUE`: `LenCondition`/`ArrayContainsCondition`/`MapHasKeyCondition` now emit bracket-access chained-guard syntax; added an `AbsentOrEmptyCondition` fallback.
- Added `conditionUsesChainedGuard` helper. `AllConditionsCondition` and `LogicalExpr`(AND) join with `" if "` when any operand is chained-guard (else `" && "`); OR always joins `" || "`; `AndCondition` no longer wraps chained operands in `(...) && (...)`.
- `buildFieldTree`: `SetIfOp`/`SpreadIfOp` with an `AbsentOrEmptyCondition` are pre-expanded into two branch insertions → two `if` blocks.
- `writeFieldNode`: bracket-access keys now render inside guarded `if` block(s) (two for AbsentOrEmpty); unconditional keys render bare.
- `writeValidator`: refactored into `writeValidatorGuarded`/`writeValidatorBody`/`writeValidatorFail` so `FailWhen(AbsentOrEmpty)` emits two false-assignment blocks and `OnlyWhen(AbsentOrEmpty)` duplicates the whole body under both branches.
- `writeOneOfParam`: drops the `?` marker when both `Optional()` and a `Default` are set (concrete discriminator), keeps `?` when Optional without a default.

+package defkit
+
+import (
+	"fmt"
+	"testing"
+)
+
+func TestSpecVerify(t *testing.T) {
+	g := &CUEGenerator{indent: "\t"}
+	// LenCondition (string/array/map)
+	fmt.Println("LenGt:", g.conditionToCUE(String("name").LenGt(5)))
+	fmt.Println("ArrLenEq5:", g.conditionToCUE(Array("tags").LenEq(5)))
+	fmt.Println("Contains:", g.conditionToCUE(Array("tags").Contains("gpu")))
+	fmt.Println("HasKey:", g.conditionToCUE(Map("config").HasKey("debug")))
+	fmt.Println("IsNotEmpty:", g.conditionToCUE(Array("tags").IsNotEmpty()))
+	fmt.Println("SKM HasKey:", g.conditionToCUE(StringKeyMap("labels").HasKey("k")))
+	fmt.Printf("IsEmpty type: %T\n", Array("tags").IsEmpty())
+	fmt.Printf("ArrLenEq0 type: %T\n", Array("tags").LenEq(0))
+	fmt.Printf("SKM LenEq0 type: %T\n", StringKeyMap("l").LenEq(0))
+	// AllConditions
+	fmt.Println("AllCond chained:", g.conditionToCUE(AllConditions(String("name").IsSet(), Array("tags").LenGt(0))))
+	fmt.Println("AllCond plain:", g.conditionToCUE(AllConditions(String("name").IsSet(), Bool("b").IsTrue())))
+	fmt.Println("Or chained:", g.conditionToCUE(Or(String("name").IsSet(), Array("tags").LenGt(0))))
+	fmt.Println("And chained:", g.conditionToCUE(And(String("name").IsSet(), Array("tags").LenGt(0))))
+	// RequiredImports
+	fmt.Println("Arr imports none:", Array("x").RequiredImports())
+	fmt.Println("Arr imports min:", Array("x").MinItems(1).RequiredImports())
+	fmt.Println("Arr imports both:", Array("x").MinItems(1).MaxItems(3).RequiredImports())
+}
